title: PromptHive: Bringing Subject Matter Experts Back to the Forefront with Collaborative Prompt Engineering for Educational Content Creation
extended_summary:
This paper addresses how to involve subject matter experts (SMEs) more effectively in prompt engineering for educational content creation with large language models. The authors argue that while LLMs can help generate instructional materials, non-AI experts need interface support to systematically experiment with prompts, compare outputs, and collaborate with others. The paper introduces PromptHive, a human-centered, collaborative prompt authoring interface designed to help SMEs create prompts for generating hints in an adaptive tutoring system.

The intervention studied is PromptHive, an open-source system integrated with the OATutor workflow for college algebra content creation. The interface supports a four-stage workflow—load, author, share, and iterate—and includes tools for sampling problems, comparing prompt-output pairs, cloning prompts, and sharing effective prompt formulations. The authors evaluated the system through two linked studies: a user study with 10 mathematics SMEs who had prior OATutor authoring experience, and a learner study comparing PromptHive-generated hints with previously human-authored hints in OATutor.

The population and context span both content creators and learners. The SME study involved 10 mathematics tutors/content authors, mostly 3rd- or 4th-year undergraduates or recent graduates, participating remotely via Zoom. The learning study involved current undergraduate college students in the United States recruited through Prolific; learners completed pre-tests, tutoring tasks, and post-tests across college algebra lessons in an online environment. The content was based on OpenStax College Algebra materials used in OATutor.

The main conclusions are that PromptHive substantially improved the efficiency and usability of educational content authoring for SMEs. Participants reported excellent usability (SUS 89/100), much lower perceived cognitive workload than manual authoring, and strong feelings of control and trust while using the system. The collaborative interface helped SMEs produce prompt-generated hints judged to be comparable to human-authored materials, and the learner study was designed to compare learning gains from PromptHive-generated versus human-authored hints. Overall, the paper concludes that well-designed collaborative prompt engineering tools can enable non-AI experts to create scalable educational content much faster while maintaining educational quality.

identified_tools.name: PromptHive
identified_tools.description: An open-source collaborative prompt-authoring interface that enables subject matter experts to create, test, share, and refine prompts for LLM-generated educational content, especially hint pathways for problems in OATutor.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as a human-centered interface for mathematics subject matter experts to collaboratively author prompts that generate hints and scaffolded hints for a college algebra textbook, and to deploy those hints in OATutor for a learner learning-gain comparison against manually authored hints.

findings.finding_summary: In a user study with 10 mathematics subject matter experts, PromptHive was rated as highly usable with a System Usability Scale score of 89/100. The paper reports that the tool reduced perceived cognitive workload substantially relative to manual hint authoring, with NASA-TLX scores dropping from 55.17 to 26.73 out of 100, and reduced authoring time from several months to a few hours for textbook-scale hint creation.
findings.measure: System usability (SUS), perceived cognitive workload (NASA-TLX), authoring time

findings.finding_summary: In a learning gain study with 225 unique undergraduate participants and 549 completed lesson submissions (268 human-only, 281 PromptHive), PromptHive-generated hints produced learning gains that were on par with human-authored hints. The paper states there were no statistically significant differences between PromptHive-generated hints and the human-only authored hints control condition on learning gains.
findings.measure: Pre-test to post-test learning gains in college algebra under PromptHive-generated versus human-authored hint pathways
findings.sample_size: n=225 unique participants; 549 completed lesson submissions

quality_tier_rationale: The paper includes empirical evaluation with a learner comparison study and a structured user study, but the excerpt does not report enough statistical detail on the learning-gain design or effect estimates to justify blue. Evidence is stronger than purely qualitative work because it includes comparative outcome data with learners.
impact_tier_rationale: Operational efficiency and usability impacts are clearly positive, but academic impact appears equivalent rather than superior to human-authored hints, and no effect sizes are reported. Overall impact is promising but unclear in magnitude for student learning.
